content.comment_body: The light is intended to blink every 3 seconds, continuously. Over a year, this would result in nearly 10 million cycles. While solid-state outputs seem suited for this, can the [product_name] models with solid-state outputs reliably support such frequent switching? Is there a more effective solution?
To clarify, there aren't any [product_name] modules equipped with SSR outputs—only those with transistor outputs.
I confused solid-state outputs with SSR outputs. Thank you. By the way, do you have any suggestions regarding the original question?
Transistor outputs are designed for such applications and should perform reliably, provided the specifications (0.3 Amps, 24V) are met.
